questions.q: What is AWS, precisely, according to this lesson?
options: A catalog of 200+ individual services — storage, compute, databases, networking, and more — available on demand and billed by actual usage
A single unified product you turn on for your whole company
A programming language for building cloud applications
A replacement for having any on-premises infrastructure at all, mandatory for every company
questions.explain: AWS isn't one thing — it's a large catalog of independent services used together.

questions.q: Why does this course avoid treating AWS services as a direct one-to-one translation of Azure's equivalents?
options: AWS has its own service boundaries, naming conventions, and idioms — some ideas transfer directly, but many don't map cleanly onto an Azure equivalent
AWS and Azure are actually identical products with different logos
Azure has no cloud concepts that overlap with AWS at all
This course assumes no student has ever heard of Azure
questions.explain: Object storage as a concept transfers, but mapping S3 directly onto Blob Storage feature-for-feature misses real differences.

questions.q: Which combination of services does this course's stack (AWS Fundamentals + AWS Data Engineering) build toward, per this lesson?
options: S3, Glue, Redshift, Athena, Lambda, Step Functions, Kinesis, DMS, EMR, and CloudWatch — the exact combination real AWS data engineering postings ask for
Only EC2 and general-purpose compute services
A random assortment of AWS services with no real job-market relevance
Services exclusively related to AWS machine learning, not data engineering
questions.explain: This is explicitly the real, job-posting-driven service combination this course and its follow-on are built around.

questions.q: What is this specific course's (AWS Fundamentals) job, compared to AWS Data Engineering?
options: Teaching the cloud and AWS fundamentals — accounts, IAM, networking, cost — that AWS Data Engineering's real depth assumes you already have
Teaching the same content as AWS Data Engineering, just in less detail
Teaching only AWS's machine learning services
Replacing the need for AWS Data Engineering entirely
questions.explain: AWS Fundamentals is explicitly the foundation course; AWS Data Engineering is where the real service depth lives.

questions.q: When did AWS launch, and what is its market position today, per this lesson?
options: 2006, and it remains the largest public cloud provider by market share
2015, and it is a minor, niche cloud provider
1999, before cloud computing existed as a concept
AWS has no defined market position relative to other providers
questions.explain: AWS was the first major public cloud and has maintained the largest market share since.
